from.place: Proof of Lemma 07CH: Unramified localization of the corrected-coordinate map

title: Unramified localization of the corrected-coordinate map
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, n,c natural numbers, P=R[x_1,...,x_n], f_j in P, J=(f_j), C=P/J and D=C[y_1,...,y_c] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Suppose a_ij in C satisfy sum_i (partial_i f_j mod J) a_ik = delta_jk. Define the R-algebra map theta:P -> D by x_i |-> (x_i mod J) - sum_j a_ij y_j. There is g in D with constant coefficient 1 such that the composite P -> D -> D_g [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is formally unramified, meaning its relative differential module is zero [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

source.place: Proof of Lemma 07CH, corrected coordinates, Nakayama localization and fibrewise flatness; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CH

proof.text: D is finite type over R and hence over P through theta. Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.finite therefore makes M = Omega(D/P) finite over D. For an R-derivation d and an R-algebra map phi from P, prove d(phi(h)) = sum_i phi(partial_i h) d(phi(x_i)) directly by polynomial induction (constants, sums and multiplication by a variable). This replaces the polynomial differential-basis dependency.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 07CH, corrected coordinates, Nakayama localization and fibrewise flatness; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CH

proof.text: Take I = ker(constantCoeff) and Q = M/(I M). Every y_j annihilates Q. Compose the universal P-derivation with the quotient map and restrict its scalars to R. Differentiating theta(x_i) = x_i - sum_j a_ij y_j gives dx_i = sum_j a_ij dy_j in Q. Apply the polynomial chain rule to f_k, whose image in C is zero, substitute these coordinate identities, commute the finite sums and use the right-inverse identity to conclude dy_k = 0. Thus dx_i = 0. Lift any coefficient of C to P to prove its differential zero, then induct on polynomials in D to show every differential zero in Q. The universal differentials span M, proving M <= I M. The proof uses only finite sums and polynomial induction and covers empty index sets and the zero ring.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 07CH, corrected coordinates, Nakayama localization and fibrewise flatness; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CH

proof.text: Apply Submodule.exists_sub_one_mem_and_smul_eq_zero_of_fg_of_le_smul to M and I to obtain g with g - 1 in I annihilating M. Applying constantCoeff gives constantCoeff(g) = 1. Identify the stated algebra structure on D_g with the canonical localization structure. KaehlerDifferential.isLocalizedModule_map identifies Omega(D_g/P) as the localization of M. IsLocalizedModule.subsingleton_iff makes this module zero because the single element g in powers(g) annihilates every m in M. Algebra.formallyUnramified_iff finishes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_unramified_conormal_polynomial_chart (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (n c : ℕ) (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (a : Fin n → Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)) (ha : ∀ j k, ∑ i, Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) (MvPolynomial.pderiv i (f j)) * a i k = if j = k then 1 else 0) : let C := MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f) let D := MvPolynomial (Fin c) C let θ : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] D := MvPolynomial.aeval (fun i ↦ MvPolynomial.C (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) (MvPolynomial.X i)) - ∑ j, MvPolynomial.C (a i j) * MvPolynomial.X j) ∃ g : D, MvPolynomial.constantCoeff g = 1 ∧ @FormallyUnramified (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (Localization.Away g) _ _ (((IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R D (Localization.Away g)).comp θ).toRingHom.toAlgebra)
